definition: Very careful to do things correctly and honestly, with close attention to every detail.
example: She kept scrupulous notes on every seedling in the school greenhouse, recording its height each morning.
nuance: Meticulous describes only care with details, but scrupulous also suggests a moral concern with honesty and doing what is right.
prompt: A chemist is writing up the results of a month of experiments.
options: The scrupulous chemist reported the failed trials alongside the successful ones.
The scrupulous chemist quietly deleted the readings that contradicted her theory.
The scrupulous chemist guessed at several measurements because the deadline was near.
The scrupulous chemist assumed that all of her colleagues were faking their data.
reasons: Including results that look bad shows honesty and care about keeping the full record.
Hiding inconvenient data is dishonest, which is the reverse of the word's meaning.
Guessing to save time is sloppy; the word calls for exactness.
Distrusting others is not the same as holding yourself to high standards.

practice.prompt: A student is writing a research paper that quotes several books.
options: The scrupulous student cited the page number for every quotation she used.
The scrupulous student copied whole paragraphs and presented them as her own writing.
The scrupulous student finished the paper in ten minutes without checking a single fact.
The scrupulous student was so shy that she rarely raised her hand in class.
reasons: Crediting each source precisely reflects both care and honesty about others' work.
Passing off borrowed words as your own is dishonest, so the word does not fit.
Rushing and skipping every check shows carelessness, not close attention.
Shyness is a personality trait and has nothing to do with careful, honest work.
